Hey, do not touch my daughter!
Right now we are taking these two.
We are leaving the restaurant quickly.
You sit quietly and do not make noise.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, this is just an ordinary bolt.
Tell me, who cooked this?
Obviously, this is a clever con artist.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'dish' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The dish is served with delicious pears.
This dish is simply utterly divine!

examples.text: Я шеф, и это моё блюдо.
examples.trans: I am the chef, and this is my dish.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: They simply do not want to pay!
Elena Pavlovna asked us to take care of you!
That is simply a great idea, Dad!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овершенно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: This dish is simply utterly divine!

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town.
This is a completely new car.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: This dish is simply utterly divine!
This is divine.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'читать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'consider', paired with 'посчитать'.

examples.text: Считайте, что звезда у вас в кармане.
examples.trans: Consider the star in your pocket.
You can't count.
I think you're right.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Obviously, this is a clever con artist.
Wait, did he pay the money after all?

examples.text: Он подтвердил, что он отец Кости.
examples.trans: He confirmed that he is Kostya's father.

meanings.en: star (in the sky, hotel rating, or famous person)
meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'a star' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Без меня вы звезду не получите.
examples.trans: Without me you will never get a star.
Which one of us needs the star?
The star is already almost ours!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Без меня вы звезду не получите.
examples.trans: Without me you will never get a star.

examples.text: На два часа я её уговорил.
examples.trans: I talked her into two hours a day.
A guest found a piece of metal in the soup.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Без меня вы звезду не получите.
examples.trans: Without me you will never get a star.
Just do not get nervous right now.

examples.text: Скажите, вы на самом деле инвалид?
examples.trans: Tell me, are you really disabled?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Без меня вы звезду не получите.
examples.trans: Without me you will never get a star.

examples.text: А Елена Павловна разве не против?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'pocket' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Считайте, что звезда у вас в кармане.
examples.trans: Consider the star in your pocket.
When there is no money in your pocket.
He put the keys in his pocket.

meanings.en: to happen, take place, go on
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'исходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is happening', paired with 'произойти'.

examples.trans: Why is this happening to me?
What is happening, call the police quickly!
What is going on? I don't understand.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'faster', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It is necessary, come on, open up quickly.
Quickly bring back my wheelchair!
Sit back down in your places quickly, both of you!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to call', paired with 'позвать'.

examples.trans: What's your name?
My name is Lyosha.
Mum is calling you.

meanings.note: Borrowed in the Petrine era from German 'Polizei' / French 'police' (from Greek 'politeia', civil administration).

examples.trans: I will report this to the police right now!
What is happening, call the police quickly!
Thank you for not telling the police officers.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Без меня вы звезду не получите.
examples.trans: Without me you will never get a star.

examples.text: На два часа я её уговорил.
examples.trans: I talked her into two hours a day.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'would', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, this is just an ordinary bolt.
Once I too was a chef.
I wanted the two of you to get married.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Без меня вы звезду не получите.
examples.trans: Without me you will never get a star.

examples.text: А Елена Павловна разве не против?
examples.trans: And is Elena Pavlovna not against it?
No, she is not against it at all.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to become', paired with 'становиться'.

examples.trans: She is elderly, she could have mixed it up.
No, better to let him stay at home.
For the test we need to take saliva.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, this is just an ordinary bolt.
Tell me, who cooked this?
Obviously, this is a clever con artist.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: We need to do a paternity test.

examples.text: Я об этом в кино видела.
examples.trans: I saw about that in the movies.
Tell me, what is going on here?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

examples.trans: It is necessary, come on, open up quickly.
Quickly bring back my wheelchair!

meanings.en: to stand up, to get up (out of bed)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'тать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'stood still, stopped', paired with 'вставать'.

examples.text: Может, ты сейчас встанешь со стула?
examples.trans: Maybe you will stand up from the chair now?
Everyone stand against the wall quickly!

examples.text: Кто первый встал, того и тапки.
examples.trans: First come, first served (whoever got up first gets the slippers).

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to, towards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: A guest found a piece of metal in the soup.
Tell me, who cooked this?
It does not matter who exactly cooked it.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тена'). Common feminine noun meaning 'wall' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Эй, стой на месте сейчас же!
examples.trans: Hey, stop right there this instant!
Everyone stand against the wall quickly!
This is an old wall.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А Елена Павловна разве не против?
examples.trans: And is Elena Pavlovna not against it?
No, she is not against it at all.

examples.text: На два часа я её уговорил.
examples.trans: I talked her into two hours a day.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: No, she is not against it at all.

examples.text: На два часа я её уговорил.
examples.trans: I talked her into two hours a day.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'as a cook' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He has already ruined many chefs.
Good afternoon, who is the chef here?
Believe me, I know what that is like.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'disabled person' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Скажите, вы на самом деле инвалид?
examples.trans: Tell me, are you really disabled?
Well, how am I a disabled person to you?

examples.text: Инвалид пусть тихо сидит в кресле.
examples.trans: Let the disabled man sit quietly in his chair.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'let (them)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Let both of us go right now!

examples.text: Инвалид пусть тихо сидит в кресле.
examples.trans: Let the disabled man sit quietly in his chair.
Let them build.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: You are staying here to guard these two.
Sit here completely quietly!

examples.text: Инвалид пусть тихо сидит в кресле.
examples.trans: Let the disabled man sit quietly in his chair.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'идеть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is sitting', paired with 'посидеть'.

examples.text: Папа согласился посидеть сегодня с ребёнком.
examples.trans: Dad agreed to babysit the child today.
Why are you sitting in the corner?
I'm sitting in a café.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'armchair, chair' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Инвалид пусть тихо сидит в кресле.
examples.trans: Let the disabled man sit quietly in his chair.
Sitting in my chair?

examples.text: Ты там как? В моём кресле сидишь?
examples.trans: How are you doing over there? Sitting in my chair?

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'look', paired with 'смотреть'.

examples.text: Я хочу посмотреть, как вы готовите.
examples.trans: I want to watch how you cook.
May I have a look?
I only had a look.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'колько').

examples.text: Мы с тобой сколько инспекций прошли!
examples.trans: How many inspections you and I have been through!

examples.text: Посмотри, скольким людям ты принёс проблемы.
examples.trans: Look how many people you brought trouble to.
So much gum!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'to people' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: That means this man is a sly swindler!

examples.text: Вы выдавали себя за другого человека.
examples.trans: You passed yourself off as another person.
What do you mean, as another person?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты же сама его недавно нашла.
examples.trans: You found him recently yourself, after all.
Yes, I get tired, there is a lot of work.
Yes, you tried very hard.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'brought', paired with 'приносить'.

examples.trans: What did you bring into the flat?
He brought you a dog.

examples.text: А я вот вам чаю с сушками принёс.
examples.trans: I've brought you some tea and bread rings.

meanings.note: Borrowed via Polish/German from Greek 'problema' (something thrown forward, a task or question).

examples.text: Посмотри, скольким людям ты принёс проблемы.
examples.trans: Look how many people you brought trouble to.
That's not a problem.
I have a problem.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well, what kind of maniac is he?
For the test we need to take saliva.
And I read that hair is needed.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'touch', paired with 'тронуть'.

examples.text: А ну не трогай мою дочь!
examples.trans: Hey, do not touch my daughter!
Don't touch me!
Don't touch the car.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Wait, who just came home?
I was just getting ready to go home.
Yes, it is time for me to go home too.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning '(our) daughter' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А ну не трогай мою дочь!
examples.trans: Hey, do not touch my daughter!
For my daughter I will tear anyone apart!

examples.text: Потому что я люблю свою дочь.
examples.trans: Because I love my daughter.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: Right now I will go sort it out myself.
Just do not get nervous right now.
Right now you are our main ingredient.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: He is their very chief inspector.
Because of an injury I had to leave the profession.
You recently came out of a coma.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'бирать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'we are taking', paired with 'забрать'.

examples.trans: Right now we are taking these two.
I pick the children up from school.
You take all the money.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'two (people)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You are staying here to guard these two.
You two are not going anywhere alone!
Right now we are taking these two.

meanings.en: to leave, to go away (on foot)
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'are leaving', paired with 'уйти'.

examples.trans: We are leaving the restaurant quickly.
I'm going home.
You are. Go away.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from/out of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Гость в супе из чечевицы нашёл.
examples.trans: The guest found it in the lentil soup.
This is a Michelin inspector from Paris!
His legs were completely paralyzed.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: Viktor decided to open his own restaurant.
We are leaving the restaurant quickly.

examples.text: Но его ресторан достоин получить звезду.
examples.trans: But his restaurant is worthy of receiving a star.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Без меня вы звезду не получите.
examples.trans: Without me you will never get a star.

examples.text: А Елена Павловна разве не против?
examples.trans: And is Elena Pavlovna not against it?
No, she is not against it at all.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'make noise'.

examples.trans: Don't make noise!
The children are noisy.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Wait, did he pay the money after all?
Yes, he paid, of course.
Thank you for your answer.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('any').

examples.text: Виктор не любит об этом говорить.
examples.trans: Viktor does not like to talk about this.
Look how much the child loves him.
I truly loved her very much.

порвать.gloss: to tear up; (slang) to blow away, break (the internet)

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'рвать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to tear up; (slang) to blow away, break (the internet)', paired with 'рвать'.

examples.trans: You broke the whole internet!
He accidentally tore the letter.

examples.text: Ты весь интернет порвал! Сосед твой — народный герой!
examples.trans: You broke the whole internet! Your neighbour is a national hero!
